concerns.text: Task T008a sets a hard fail-fast threshold at RAM > 6.5GB. This silently weakens the Constitution Principle VII and Spec SC-003 which mandate verification against the 7GB limit. A run using 6.8GB would be valid per spec but fail per task, violating the constraint preservation rule.

Task T033 allows a sample size of 'all available if < 50'. Spec FR-010 mandates a sample of 50 tasks. This relaxation removes the statistical power guarantee required by the spec's Assumptions (margin of error ≤ 10%), constituting a silent weakening of the acceptance criteria.

Task T033c is defined as a 'Manual Annotation Gate' placeholder. The pipeline cannot proceed to T034/T034b without this manual step. This introduces a silent drift from the Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires the project to be 'runnable end-to-end without manual intervention' on a fresh runner.

Phase 5.5 tasks require statistical comparison of 'learning rates' and 'search vs. learning' against a baseline. The Plan explicitly restricts the monolithic baseline to a local Phi-3-mini (no external API). Without a true external baseline (e.g., GPT-4) to distinguish 'static library search' from 'state modification', the tasks cannot satisfy the research question, weakening the core hypothesis validation.

Task T030 halts execution if power < 0.80. However, T013 (filtering) has no upstream guarantee of producing a dataset large enough to satisfy this power requirement. This creates a deterministic failure path where the spec's power analysis requirement (FR-011) cannot be met, effectively weakening the feasibility of the experiment.
